t: You're looking at the Roundhouse, a performing arts and concert venue in Chalk Farm, in a Grade II* listed former railway engine shed. The London & North Western Railway built it in 1846 to 1847 as a roundhouse, a circular building holding a railway turntable. It was used for that purpose for only about a decade. After years as a warehouse, it fell into disuse just before the Second World War. Robert Stephenson, the engineer and locomotive designer, son of George Stephenson, the Father of Railways, designed it.
